extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, consisting of 8 languages with about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish), suitable for speech research including ASR and TTS.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by (i) training acoustic models on in-house data, (ii) generating pseudo-labels with these models on LibriVox audiobooks, and (iii) retrieving original transcripts by matching pseudo-labels to available book transcripts from Project Gutenberg. Audio files were downloaded from LibriVox using LibriLight open source library tools, downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz, and segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox with corresponding text transcripts from Project Gutenberg books. The raw audio files had huge variance in duration from few minutes to hours at 48kHz sampling rate. For acoustic model training, in-house datasets consisting of audio from videos publicly shared by users were used (completely de-identified).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Trained acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss for audio segmentation; wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MLS is a read-speech dataset derived from audiobooks, which may limit its generalization to other speech domains. The dataset leverages LibriVox audiobook data, most of which is based on Project Gutenberg text data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for speech research, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. Train, development and test splits and limited supervision train sets are provided.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be made freely available under an open license at http://www.openslr.org. LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data are released in the public domain, which allows free release to everyone.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: SpecAugment data augmentation with two frequency masks and ten time masks with maximum time mask ratio of p = 0.1; frequency and time mask parameters tuned separately for each model; time warping not used. Maximum frequency bands masked by one frequency mask is 30, and maximum frames masked by time mask is 30. Books filtered to avoid overlap with development and test sets using edit distance and 5-gram inverted index matching.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with TDS Convolutions and ASG loss. Segmentation performed via streaming inference generating viterbi token sequences with timestamps. Audio converted to 80-channel log-mel filterbanks as input features.

We have also carefully filtered certain books to avoid any overlap with the development and test sets, following the procedure described in [13].
